correctness.rationale: Every exponent is 2^s-1 because τ(n) is 2-primary. Geometric factorization and the multiplicative-order exact 2-adic valuation prove that no odd numerator prime has small ν2(ℓ−1). Protected odd denominator exponents therefore exactly encode kν_q(n); equality recovers the odd part. Strict growth in the 2-power exponent recovers the even part; 1≤σ_{−k}(n)<2 matches fractional parts. Verified n=1 and both parities. Exact finite checker run over n≤30000, k=2,4,6,8,12 passes but is not the proof.

value.rationale: Provides an unbounded infinite family of verified injectivity in a concrete open fractional-part problem for every even k, with exact denominator prime-support decoding and no bounded prime-count condition. The protected residue classes and 2-primary exponent restriction arise from the unavoidable cyclotomic factorization, not an arbitrary finite search slice; the result leaves the global conjecture open.
